Respecting the Khalifahs and Ameers and Obeying their Commands
The Incident that occurred between Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) and Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) During an Expedition

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once dispatched Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed bin Mughiera Makhzoomi on expedition. With him was Hadhrat Ammaar bin Yaasir (RA). The expedition left and finally drew close to the people whom they intended to ambush early in the morning. They set up camp there late at night. However, someone warned the people (about the presence of the Sahabah (RA)) and they all fled to a place of safety. One of the men amongst them who had accepted Islaam together with his family stayed behind. He instructed his family to load their goods and then told them to wait until he returned.
He then proceeded to meet Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) and said, "O Abu Yaqdhaan! My family and I have accepted Islaam. Will this help me if I stay behind (in the town) because all my people had fled when they heard about your arrival?" Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) said to him, "You may stay behind, for you are safe." The man and his family then went back. When Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) launched the attack the next morning, he found that the people had all fled. He then captured the man and his family. Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) said, "You can do nothing to a man who has accepted Islaam." Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) said, "What have you to do with this? When I am the Ameer, how could you grant a person amnesty without my permission?" Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) replied, "I can indeed grant amnesty without your permission even though you are the Ameer. This man has accepted Imaan and if he wished to, he could have left with the others. Because he has Imaan, I instructed him to stay behind." The two Sahabah (RA) then argued until they started abusing each other.
When they returned to Madinah, they both went to Rasulullaah ﷺ and Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) told him about the man and what he had done. Rasulullaah ﷺ then authorised the amnesty that Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) had granted but at the same time also forbade people from granting amnesty to others without the permission of the Ameer.
